chunks: Yunus from Hisham ibn Ibrahim al-Mashriqi, from one who narrated it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would administer flogging for a small amount of nabidh (fermented drink) just as he would for a small amount of khamr (wine), and would execute for the third pouring of nabidh just as he would for the third pouring of khamr.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin (Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الثَّالِثَة: The third (referring to the third pouring or measure in the context of fermentation/intoxication)
key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Nabidh (fermented drink, typically from dates or barley)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for drinking nabidh according to Amir al-Mu'minin?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar highlights the juristic principle of 'qalil wa kathir' (small and large quantities) in the consumption of nabidh, demonstrating that Ali ibn Abi Talib applied the same penal hierarchy to nabidh as to khamr. The reference to the 'third' likely alludes to the third pouring of water over the fruit, a point of contention among Shia scholars regarding when nabidh transitions from permissible to intoxicating and thus incurs the hadd punishment of execution.
